title: Two Kepler short-cadence months lack the target-mode amplitude required for a steady 552.16 microHz alias
abstract: We test whether a steady target pulsation near 552.16 microHz can explain the known 19.48-hour KIC 10001893 signal through long-cadence sampling. Two Kepler release 25 short-cadence months give fitted fast amplitudes of 18 to 29 ppm. The largest approximate pointwise 99 percent amplitude radius is 102 ppm across two flux products, two trend lengths and two noise-block lengths. Frame integration requires about 1122 ppm in short cadence to produce 29 ppm in long cadence at equal dilution. Header crowding estimates still require at least 946 ppm for a target mode. Added 1122 ppm signals recover at 1103 to 1141 ppm over 32 phase trials. These data argue against this steady target-mode alias under a linear response and the stated noise assumptions. They do not confirm a planet or a new signal. A variable fast mode, nearby source and other stellar or instrument causes remain open. The two cadences share a telescope. Code, aggregate fits, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Fast-mode fitted amplitudes and approximate pointwise upper radii in two short-cadence months. The red line is the amplitude required for a 29 ppm long-cadence alias at equal dilution. Labels give quarter, flux product, trend days and noise-block days. Products and variants share exposures.

citations.reason: Provides the open coherent fast-alias hypothesis and required long-cadence amplitude. We test it with short-cadence data.
